If you've ever needed thirty puzzles by Friday, you know the routine.

Word searches are the easiest thing in the world to use — and one of the most tedious things to make. That gap is where whole evenings disappear.

You're placing letters by hand

A blank 15×15 grid, a word list, and a pencil. Then you hunt for accidental words you didn't mean to create, and start again.

You're renting your puzzles

Printable marketplaces bill you every month whether or not they have the topic you actually need this week — and you can't change the grid, the font, or the size.

Your book is stuck at 12 pages

You have an idea for a low-content book. What you don't have is 100 pages of clean, consistent interiors and an answer key for each one.

Here's the part that stings: none of this is hard work. It's slow work. Every puzzle needs the same six decisions — grid size, word list, directions, filler, layout, answer key — and you're making them by hand, one at a time, over and over.

That's the job this app does for you, in seconds, without anything to install.

The whole thing is one file

Pick a topic. Pick a style. Export.

Word Search Empire is a single HTML file. You open it in your browser and everything runs on your own machine — there's no login, no API key, no upload, and no monthly fee. Turn off your Wi‑Fi and it still works.

Choose one of the 24 themed word banks and it drops in a fresh random set of words. Choose a grid size and difficulty, then watch the real page preview update instantly. When it looks right, export it. If you want a whole book, the book builder lays out 5 to 120 puzzles with the answer keys grouped at the back — the layout paperback buyers already expect.

You bring the topic. It does the layout, the grid, the filler letters and the answer key.

Every word list is already written

The topic dashboard holds 24 themed word banks, sorted into seven categories — Food & Drink, Animals & Nature, Seasons & Outdoors, Holidays, Places & Travel, Fun & Play, and Learning & Life.

Each bank contains 10,000 words, deduplicated and filtered down to the three-to-fifteen letter lengths that actually fit a puzzle grid. Tap a card and a fresh random set drops straight into the puzzle — tap it again and you get a completely different set from the same theme, which is how you build forty different pages that don't repeat themselves.

What's inside

Not a feature list — the reason each one matters when you're actually making something.

  • 24 thematic word banks, 10,000 words each. Generate a whole themed book without writing a single word list. The banks are deduplicated, spell-checked and filtered to the 3–15 letter sweet spot for grids.
  • Paste your own words from anywhere. Type or paste a list separated by line breaks or commas — including straight out of an AI chat — and it strips badges, numbers and symbols for you.
  • Grids from 8×8 to 25×25. One app covers a six-year-old's worksheet and a large-print adult puzzle, with Easy, Medium, Hard and Expert presets.
  • Eight toggleable directions. Across, down, two diagonals, and every one of them backwards — so you can dial difficulty exactly where you want it.
  • Filler control. Random A–Z normally, vowel-heavy when you want it easier, rare letters when you want it mean.
  • Five one-click styles. Classic, Playful, Elegant, Bold and Chalkboard — then fine-tune cell shape, title font, paper colour, letter colour, highlight colour and grid border.
  • Four print trims. US Letter 8.5×11, 8×10, 6×9 and A4 — the exact sizes KDP and printable marketplaces expect, with the page size applied to the printed output too.
  • 300-DPI PNG export. Puzzle and answer key export as print-resolution images you can drop straight into a listing, a workbook or a print shop order.
  • Bulk book builder. Build 5 to 120 puzzles in one pass: puzzles one per page, answer keys grouped four to a page at the back, your book title in the header of every page, and page numbers down the footer.
  • Print or save as PDF. Send a single worksheet to the printer, or save a complete interior as a PDF manuscript ready for upload.
  • Your branding, not mine. Put your press name, author name or copyright line in the footer — the files you export look like yours.
  • Numbered pages and uppercase banks. The small details that separate a book that looks published from one that looks photocopied.

Five styles to start from

Same puzzle engine, five very different books. Pick a preset, then change anything you like — nothing is locked to a template.

Change the paper, letter colour, grid colour, highlight colour, cell shape, title font, word-bank style and border weight independently. A kids' activity sheet, a large-print senior book and a Christmas gift printable are all the same app with different settings.

The part that saves the most time

A whole book, laid out in one pass

Tell it how many puzzles you want and where the words should come from — a rotating set of themes for variety, your own list, or a mix of both. Then hit build.

The book builder produces puzzles one per page, groups the answer keys four to a page at the back, puts your book title in the header of every page, and numbers the whole thing. Print it to PDF and you have an interior manuscript instead of a folder of loose images.

Want fifty pages? Want one hundred and twenty? The minimum is five and the maximum is 120 puzzles in a single build.

Questions people actually ask

Do I need internet, an account, or a subscription?

None of the three. It's a single file that runs in your browser. There's no login, no activation, no API key and no server. Download it once and it works offline. You pay once; there is no recurring charge.

What do I need to run it?

Any modern browser — Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox — on Windows, Mac or Linux. Double-click the file and it opens. There's nothing to install and no technical setup.

Is this AI? Does it send my words anywhere?

No. It's a deterministic puzzle engine — the same algorithm builds the grid, places the words, fills the gaps and writes the answer key every time. Nothing is uploaded and no data leaves your computer. It also means the results are predictable and repeatable rather than random nonsense.

Can I sell the puzzles and books I make?

Yes — that's the point. The puzzles, pages, books and exports you create are yours to print, distribute and sell. Use the built-in word banks, paste your own lists, or combine them.

Is it built for KDP and printable shops?

It's built around their formats. The trim sizes are US Letter 8.5×11, 8×10, 6×9 and A4 — the sizes used by paperback interiors and printable listings — and the page size is applied to the actual printed output, not just the preview. You get puzzles one-per-page and answer keys grouped at the back, plus a PDF export you can save as a manuscript.

What if the topic I need isn't one of the 24?

Paste your own word list. Type or paste words separated by line breaks or commas — from a notebook, a spreadsheet, or straight out of an AI chat — and the app cleans them up automatically. Anything spelled in the A–Z alphabet will work.

How long does one puzzle take?

The grid generates as fast as you can click. Choosing a topic, setting the size and exporting takes about as long as reading this sentence. A 50-puzzle book interior takes a few seconds to build and a moment to scroll through — the slow part is deciding which style you prefer.

Do I get the answer keys?

Yes, automatically — for every puzzle, in every book, with every hidden word highlighted in colour so the answers jump out. You never build an answer key by hand.

What exactly do I receive, and when?

Immediately after checkout you'll get a download link for the app file plus the two bonus PDFs. Checkout and delivery are handled by WarriorPlus, so your receipt and download link come from them.

What if I don't like it?

Email support within 14 days with your receipt and you'll be refunded in full. The full policy is linked in the footer, and it's short because there isn't much to it.
